title: Typography / Large-format scale — 1x table

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: 1x

slide_intent: Establish a baseline before enlarging typography, because relative size and line height need to remain coordinated across scripts.
strategic_value: A complete shared scale can help IBM teams select type consistently instead of inventing a new hierarchy for every format.
demonstration: The selected 1x tab shows the full three-column table: default sizes 6–300, adjusted sizes at 95%, and corresponding line heights with alternatives for some smaller sizes.
practical_value: Look up a baseline size and its script-adjusted counterpart before applying a large-format multiplier.

content_islands.name: Default and adjusted sizes
content_islands.spec: Align the default-script sizes with the 95% adjusted values in the first two columns.

content_islands.name: Line-height options
content_islands.spec: Keep the line-height column aligned with each size, preserving multiple options where shown.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying type-scale guidance explains that shared size/line-height relationships maintain coherence and accommodate differing script anatomy.
reference_purposes.Application: The complete 1x table provides coordinated default, adjusted and line-height values.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying guidance assigns 95% point sizes to Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Devanagari and Arabic while retaining the same line heights.
